endorsements.quote: if physicians choose to use experimental or transition phase AI technologies, informed consent may require more attention to the experimental nature as well as the known and unknown risks that AI introduces into the planned treatment.

In addition to information about recognized risks that are reasonably expected to impact the planned treatment, patients should also receive information about unknown risks of experimental treatments as well as viable alternative treatments, particularly when they present different risk profiles th an the chosen treatment .

Instead on focusing on information for disclosure’s sake, informed consent discussions should remain focused on empowering patient autonomy by providing information that is relevant to patients ’ decisions in situations when patients have a meaningful choice .

unlisted_practices: Ensure physicians have sufficient training and information about the evidence, performance, limitations, and conditions for use of AI-driven tools to remain trusted experts within the patient-doctor relationship.
Disclose viable established AI-based alternatives with distinct advantages or materially different risk-benefit profiles to patients when a clinician chooses not to use them.

screen.reason: This is a perspective article examining legal cases to offer insights and recommendations regarding patient informed consent and AI integration into clinical practice.
